questions.def: Neither refers to two, while none refers to more than two.
questions.question: ___ of the applicants had the required experience.

questions.def: Couldn't expresses impossibility or disbelief in the past.
questions.question: I ___ have imagined such a beautiful sight.

questions.def: "Not any" is incorrect. Use "none" or "not one".
questions.question: Not any of the students were present.

questions.def: "Unbelievable" is the correct negative adjective form.
questions.question: I found his explanation completely ___.

questions.def: "Never" emphasizes that he did not show up at all.
questions.question: He said he would be here, but he ___ showed up.

questions.def: "No point" is the correct idiom to express futility.
questions.question: There is ___ point in arguing about it now.

questions.def: Double negatives are incorrect. Should be "anything".
questions.question: He doesn't know nothing about it.

questions.def: "Disapproved" is the correct negative verb form.
questions.question: The council ___ the building plans.

questions.def: "Never" emphasizes the negative experience of seeing the film.
questions.question: I have ___ seen such a terrible film before.

questions.def: "None" is correct because it refers to more than two people.
questions.question: ___ of us wanted to go to the party.

questions.def: After "didn't," use the base form: "use to."
questions.question: She didn't used to like coffee.

questions.def: "Ununderstandable" is the most natural negative adjective.
questions.question: I found his accent completely ___.

questions.def: "No longer" is the correct phrase to indicate cessation.
questions.question: He is ___ longer working at the company.

questions.def: "Shouldn't have" expresses regret about a past action.
questions.question: I ___ have gone there without telling you.

questions.def: Avoid double negatives. Use "anything" after "isn't".
questions.question: There isn't nothing we can do about it.

questions.def: "Disobedience" is the correct negative noun form.
questions.question: His ___ of the rules led to his dismissal.

questions.def: "Not one" emphasizes the lack of helpers.
questions.question: There was ___ one person who offered to help.

questions.def: "No intention" is the idiomatic way to express lack of intent.
questions.question: I have ___ intention of going to that meeting.

questions.def: Avoid double negatives. Use "anywhere" after "never".
questions.question: He has never been nowhere near here.

questions.def: "Unsatisfactory" is the correct and most common negative adjective.
questions.question: The results were ___.

questions.def: "Neither" is used when referring to exactly two options.
questions.question: ___ of my parents are still alive.

questions.def: "No use" is the correct idiom for futile effort.
questions.question: It's ___ use trying to convince him.

questions.def: Avoid double negatives. "Nobody" should be "anybody."
questions.question: I haven't seen nobody all day.

questions.def: "Resistance" is correct, implying the *lack* of submission.
questions.question: The country faced ___ during the occupation.

questions.def: "No remorse" expresses a complete lack of regret.
questions.question: He showed ___ remorse for his actions.

questions.def: "Shouldn't have" shows regret about a past action.
questions.question: I ___ have agreed to that. It was a mistake.

questions.def: "None" when referring to uncountable nouns takes singular verb.
questions.question: None of the money were recovered.

questions.def: "Irresponsibly" is the correct negative adverb form.
questions.question: He acted ___.

questions.def: "No need" is idiomatic for indicating absence of necessity.
questions.question: There is ___ need to panic.

questions.def: "Couldn't help" is the fixed expression showing involuntariness.
questions.question: I ___ help but laugh at his joke.
